items.title: 研究揭示人工繁育绿孔雀骨骼畸形诱因
items.summary: 中新网昆明9月21日电 (陆琳)近日，云南森林自然中心(云南省野生动植物救护繁育中心)与云南农业大学动物医学院合作的研究成果《天然植物来源肠道代谢物缺乏可能是圈养绿孔雀(Pavo muticus)出现骨骼畸形的潜在诱因》在国际学术期刊《Animals》正式发表，揭示了迁地保护条件下，人工繁育绿孔雀骨骼畸形的重要潜在诱因，为提升人工繁育质量、推动野化放归提供科学支撑。

items.summary: 今年5月，中国青年报社社会调查中心针对应届毕业生的调查显示，64.1%的受访者期待企业更加注重人才培养，提供完善的岗前培训与成长支持。在人工智能快速进入招聘、办公和专业服务场景的背景下，这个期待值得认真理解。人们常把AI对就业的影响概括为“哪些岗位会增加、哪些岗位会减少”，但对刚进入劳动力市场的年轻人来说，还有一个更具体的问题：当文案整理、资料搜集、基础分析、简单编码等入门任务越来越多地由AI完成，年轻人究竟通过什么任务积累最初的工作经验？

items.title: Expert team to drive improvements in cancer care
items.summary: Expert cancer board to scrutinise progress on faster diagnosis, treatment and care. People with rare cancers, children and young people to have dedicated national voices. First meeting today to drive delivery of the government’s National Ca
items.bodyHtml:
• Expert cancer board to scrutinise progress on faster diagnosis, treatment and care.
  • People with rare cancers, children and young people to have dedicated national voices.
  • First meeting today to drive delivery of the government’s National Cancer Plan.

People with cancer will benefit from stronger national leadership to improve diagnosis, treatment and care, as the reformed National Cancer Board meets for the first time today.

It will scrutinise progress against more than 100 commitments in the National Cancer Plan – including early diagnosis, treatment and quality of life - identifying which areas are falling behind and advising ministers on where further action is needed to ensure every patient receives the best possible care.

The board will have dedicated expert leads for rare cancers, including brain tumours, children and young people with cancer, and inequalities in cancer care.

It builds on the government’s progress to improve cancer care, with all three cancer standards better than a year ago and around 250,000 more people over the last year getting diagnosed on time or having cancer ruled out, compared to the year before the election.

Health and Social Care Secretary Yvette Cooper said:

Most families are affected by cancer at some point in our lives. That is why our National Cancer Plan is so important to provide earlier diagnosis, more advanced treatment and improve outcomes for everyone affected by cancer.

The newly established, independent National Cancer Board will help scrutinise our progress, identify the areas that need most attention, and ensure the voice of cancer patients is constantly heard.

I look forward to working with Anita Charlesworth and her team to deliver the change that every person in our country wants to see, and from which millions of our loved ones will benefit in the years to come.

Independent co-chair Anita Charlesworth will lead the board alongside Mark Cubbon, from NHS England and Department of Health and Social Care, giving patients and the public confidence that progress is being properly scrutinised and held to account.

She will be joined by:

  • Dr Rob Metcalf, clinical lead for rare cancers
  • Dr Dianne Addei, lead for inequalities
  • Ashley Ball-Gamble, lead for children and young people’s cancers. 

The board will meet every quarter and will publish an annual assessment of progress, with a more detailed review after three years to identify where the plan needs to be strengthened or refreshed.

Anita Charlesworth, independent co-chair of the National Cancer Board, said:

Half of us will be diagnosed with cancer during our lives, so this matters profoundly to patients and families right across the country.

The National Cancer Plan is rightly ambitious, and this Board will maintain a relentless focus on earlier diagnosis and making sure innovation reaches every patient, no matter who they are or where they live.

I look forward to working with my fellow members to ensure the National Cancer Board is a force for progress.

Professor Peter Johnson, national clinical director for cancer at NHS England, said:

Our national cancer plan sets out how we will deliver world-class care for cancer patients.

Bringing together clinical experts, charity leaders and patients to scrutinise progress will help ensure we deliver on our commitments, while dedicated leads for rare cancers, children and young people, and inequalities will give a stronger voice to those who can too often be overlooked.

The National Cancer Plan, published in February 2026, set out the government’s ambition for three in four people diagnosed with cancer to be cancer-free or living well five years after diagnosis by 2035.

Alongside improving cancer care performance, the government has also begun rolling out key commitments from the plan, including expanding access to lung cancer screening, expanding Community Diagnostic Centres, improving access to cutting-edge treatments and research, and strengthening support for children and young people, people living with and beyond cancer, and those with rare cancers.

The government has also delivered world-leading action on prevention through the Tobacco and Vapes Act which will create the first smoke-free generation, alongside targeted screening programmes and expanded access to advanced radiotherapy.

Michelle Mitchell, Chief Executive at Cancer Research UK, said:  

Delivering lasting change for people affected by cancer will require strong leadership and clear accountability. It’s encouraging to see dedicated expertise brought together to drive much-needed improvements including detecting cancer earlier, reducing unacceptable waiting times and improving access to the best treatment. 

Beating cancer means beating it for everyone, and delivering on the commitments made by the Government will be essential to improve cancer outcomes and address the challenges faced by people with cancer.

Gemma Peters, Chief Executive at Macmillan Cancer Support, said: 

The first meeting of the National Cancer Board is an important moment for turning the National Cancer Plan from ambition into action. 

The Plan set out bold commitments to improve people’s quality of life and experience of care alongside cancer outcomes. People living with cancer now need to see those commitments translated into real change. We are particularly pleased that a dedicated inequalities lead has been appointed. Embedding commitment to narrowing inequalities from the start is the only way the Plan can truly be delivered. 

Macmillan is ready to work with partners across the system to help turn the Plan’s ambitions into meaningful improvements for everyone living with cancer.

Chris Walden, CEO at Cancer52 said:  

The first meeting of the National Cancer Board marks an important step in bringing together the leadership and expertise needed to drive progress on cancer outcomes in England.  

Cancer52 is proud to bring the collective voice and experience of our member charities to the Board, helping to ensure that the distinct needs of people with rare and less common cancers remain central to its work.  

The National Cancer Plan’s dedicated focus on these cancers is a landmark commitment and we look forward to helping turn that ambition into meaningful and measurable progress for patients.

Rachel Kirby-Rider, Chief Executive at Young Lives vs Cancer said: 

Every day 12 children and young people are diagnosed with cancer, bringing many challenges that impact almost every aspect of their and their families’ lives. 

It’s historic that the National Cancer Plan includes a dedicated chapter for children and young people for the first time. We’re delighted the expert National Cancer Board has launched to lead the progress on the Plan’s commitments - including for children and young people. 

We are pleased to see the appointment of Ashley Ball-Gamble, CEO of CCLG and Chair of the Children and Young People’s Cancer Coalition, as the Board’s lead for children and young people’s cancers. He is an expert, dedicated champion of improving young cancer patients’ experiences and outcomes, and we look forward to continuing to work with him and the government to ensure children, young people and their families get the support they need when facing cancer.

Dr Sara Stoneham, Chair, CCLG: The Children & Young People’s Cancer Association, consultant paediatric and Teenage and Young Adult oncologist said: 

Following the welcome inclusion of a specific children and young people’s chapter and recommendations in the National Cancer Plan, we are pleased that the reformed National Cancer Board will include a dedicated expert lead for children and young people’s cancer. 

This important appointment will support the implementation and delivery of the children and young people’s recommendations in the National Cancer Plan, and scrutinise progress towards achieving the vital progress needed for young cancer patients and their families.  

We look forward to continuing to work with partners in government and the NHS, charities and the wider children and young people’s cancer community to ensure these ambitions become a reality.

items.title: PM call with Prime Minister Frederiksen of Denmark: 20 September 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister spoke to the Prime Minister of Denmark, Mette Frederiksen, this morning. The two leaders began by discussing their upcoming visits to New York for the UN General Assembly. The Prime Minister said he would use the trip to
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister spoke to the Prime Minister of Denmark, Mette Frederiksen, this morning.

The two leaders began by discussing their upcoming visits to New York for the UN General Assembly. The Prime Minister said he would use the trip to drive forward work on issues that matter to people at home, including reducing the cost of living through greater global stability and delivering security for people through closer international partnerships.

Turning to defence and security, the two leaders discussed the forthcoming signing of a new deal to strengthen security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area between the US, Greenland and Denmark this week.

They welcomed the US’ commitment to the region and underlined the strategic and shared importance of the High North for Euro-Atlantic security.

The Prime Minister congratulated Prime Minister Frederiksen and the Kingdom of Denmark on negotiating a deal benefitting the US, Greenland and Denmark, and said he would pass on his congratulations to President Trump.

The leaders also discussed the situation in Ukraine, and the Prime Minister said he hoped to make further progress with partners on stepping up support for Ukraine during UNGA and in the coming weeks.

The leaders agreed to stay in close touch.

items.title: Government launches National Taskforce for Tackling Misogyny
items.summary: Minister for Women and Equalities launches national taskforce to tackle the rise of misogyny Government, local leaders and experts will look at misogyny prevention across society – including community and the workplaces – so women and girls
items.bodyHtml:
• Minister for Women and Equalities launches national taskforce to tackle the rise of misogyny
  • Government, local leaders and experts will look at misogyny prevention across society – including community and the workplaces – so women and girls no longer need to face harmful attitudes
  • Bridget Phillipson: “Government will lead from the front to shift the dial and send misogynistic attitudes back to the dark ages.”

Women and girls will be better protected from harmful and dangerous attitudes, as a new national taskforce sets out to root out misogyny from across society chaired by the Minister for Women and Equalities, Bridget Phillipson.

The taskforce will bring together experts from across the country, along with ministers and local leaders, to discuss the lived experiences of women and girls ensuring government policy is shaped by those most affected by misogyny.

It will ask how the government can go further to tackle harmful attitudes wherever they emerge, including online, in workplaces, and in communities, so that women and girls can live their lives without fear of misogyny.

Members will include representatives from women’s organisations, academia, and local leaders, with the taskforce complementing existing cross-government work to halve violence against women and girls. They will focus on reducing harmful attitudes and shifting social culture, looking at what is working nationally and internationally. The first meeting of the new taskforce will focus on young people, with it later looking at workplaces, digital spaces and social cohesion. 

Bridget Phillipson MP, Minister for Women and Equalities, said:

Before I entered politics, I ran a refuge for women fleeing domestic abuse. I’ve seen first-hand the devastating impact on women and girls when harmful attitudes are tolerated and left unchallenged.

No woman should have to make her world smaller or curb her ambitions out of fear – and making that a reality is everyone’s business.

As a whole society, we can and must be better. With political leadership and the best experts from across the country, we will shift the dial on the poisonous attitudes that blight women’s lives, turn evidence into action, and send misogynistic attitudes back to the dark ages where they belong.

Gary Barker, Equimundo’s CEO and Founder said:

We’re honored to be part of the National Taskforce for Tackling Misogyny. Our research in the UK and globally shows that misogynistic attitudes are increasing – but also that they can change when men and boys are engaged as true allies in that process. 

Online and offline, too many girls and women experience harassment and abuse at the hands of men, while men and boys are also harmed by the bullying and homophobia that often accompany misogyny. 

At Equimundo, we believe that making the world safer for women and girls requires engaging all of us, and that men and boys, too, benefit from a world where women and girls can live free from harm and violence. 

This is a generational opportunity to bring men and boys into the journey toward full equality and respect for women – a journey that needs them, and that can make their own lives better, too.

Deniz Uğur, Deputy Director at the End Violence Against Women Coalition, said:

We are pleased to see the National Taskforce for Tackling Misogyny focus in on tackling the root causes of violence against women and girls (VAWG). This is especially important in supporting meaningful delivery of the VAWG Strategy, given the focus on prevention; and meeting the Government’s aim to halve VAWG in a decade.

In order to enable the work of the Taskforce to be effective, we hope to see meaningful commitment and engagement by ministers across all Government departments.

We strongly welcome the Taskforce’s consideration of how the weaponisation of VAWG fuels harm, misinformation and division in our communities, which ultimately undermines efforts to end and prevent VAWG, and ensure that victims and survivors can access support.

Tackling gender inequality and misogyny benefits our society as a whole, and is everyone’s business.

Soma Sara, CEO of Everyone’s Invited said:

Everyone’s Invited welcomes the government’s plans to introduce a Misogyny Taskforce. Sexual violence has long existed in our society, but the growth of dangerous online spaces and the rise of AI have turbocharged the scale and speed of harm.

Over 53,000 survivors have shared their experiences with us through Everyone’s Invited’s online safe space. For too many, misogyny has profoundly devastated lives.

We are particularly relieved to see a commitment to prevention through education. Young people need the tools, language and confidence to understand, question and challenge misogyny – online and offline – before it becomes normalised.

The voices of survivors and young people must be at the heart of this work, and we look forward to working with the Government to ensure this Taskforce delivers meaningful, lasting change.

Felicity Oswald, CEO of Girlguiding said:

Girlguiding is honoured to join the Minister for Women and Equalities’ new taskforce to tackle misogyny. Girls tell us they are facing rising levels of sexism and misogyny online, in public and in schools. That’s why we are calling for more education around healthy relationships, gender stereotypes, early warning signs and consent.

We welcome the opportunity to bring girls’ experiences and perspectives directly into discussions with government. Girls are experts in their own lives, and it is vital that their voices are heard when decisions are made that impact them.

Preventing misogyny before it escalates is essential. Nearly 1 million adults experience sexual assault, 1.4 million face stalking, and nearly 4 million endure domestic abuse in a single year. Tackling the source is the only viable path forward. 

This new taskforce comes ahead of further announcement expected from the government this week to step up work to halve violence and women and girls, and is the latest step by this government to use the full power of the state to tackle these vile crimes. 

Last month, the government partnered with the ENOUGH campaign at the Reading and Leeds festivals through powerful messaging raising awareness of abusive behaviours displayed over the weekend. 

The Prime Minister also recently announced that all police forces in England and Wales will have specialist rape and sexual offence teams in place by December 2027 – a year and a half ahead of the original deadline.

The government is also providing a £16 million package to tackle harmful behaviours and attitudes before they escalate, which aims to educate pupils on healthy relationships and train staff to tackle misogyny. Alongside a further £10 million fund to deliver intervention programmes for children actively using harm.

The government also published statutory relationships, sex and health education guidance for schools, challenging myths about women and relationships that are spread online in the “manosphere”.
items.bodyText:
Minister for Women and Equalities launches national taskforce to tackle the rise of misogyny
  Government, local leaders and experts will look at misogyny prevention across society – including community and the workplaces – so women and girls no longer need to face harmful attitudes
  Bridget Phillipson: “Government will lead from the front to shift the dial and send misogynistic attitudes back to the dark ages.”


Women and girls will be better protected from harmful and dangerous attitudes, as a new national taskforce sets out to root out misogyny from across society chaired by the Minister for Women and Equalities, Bridget Phillipson.

The taskforce will bring together experts from across the country, along with ministers and local leaders, to discuss the lived experiences of women and girls ensuring government policy is shaped by those most affected by misogyny.

It will ask how the government can go further to tackle harmful attitudes wherever they emerge, including online, in workplaces, and in communities, so that women and girls can live their lives without fear of misogyny.

Members will include representatives from women’s organisations, academia, and local leaders, with the taskforce complementing existing cross-government work to halve violence against women and girls. They will focus on reducing harmful attitudes and shifting social culture, looking at what is working nationally and internationally. The first meeting of the new taskforce will focus on young people, with it later looking at workplaces, digital spaces and social cohesion. 

Bridget Phillipson MP, Minister for Women and Equalities, said:


  Before I entered politics, I ran a refuge for women fleeing domestic abuse. I’ve seen first-hand the devastating impact on women and girls when harmful attitudes are tolerated and left unchallenged.

  No woman should have to make her world smaller or curb her ambitions out of fear – and making that a reality is everyone’s business.

  As a whole society, we can and must be better. With political leadership and the best experts from across the country, we will shift the dial on the poisonous attitudes that blight women’s lives, turn evidence into action, and send misogynistic attitudes back to the dark ages where they belong.


Gary Barker, Equimundo’s CEO and Founder said:


  We’re honored to be part of the National Taskforce for Tackling Misogyny. Our research in the UK and globally shows that misogynistic attitudes are increasing – but also that they can change when men and boys are engaged as true allies in that process. 

  Online and offline, too many girls and women experience harassment and abuse at the hands of men, while men and boys are also harmed by the bullying and homophobia that often accompany misogyny. 

  At Equimundo, we believe that making the world safer for women and girls requires engaging all of us, and that men and boys, too, benefit from a world where women and girls can live free from harm and violence. 

  This is a generational opportunity to bring men and boys into the journey toward full equality and respect for women – a journey that needs them, and that can make their own lives better, too.


Deniz Uğur, Deputy Director at the End Violence Against Women Coalition, said:


  We are pleased to see the National Taskforce for Tackling Misogyny focus in on tackling the root causes of violence against women and girls (VAWG). This is especially important in supporting meaningful delivery of the VAWG Strategy, given the focus on prevention; and meeting the Government’s aim to halve VAWG in a decade.

  In order to enable the work of the Taskforce to be effective, we hope to see meaningful commitment and engagement by ministers across all Government departments.

  We strongly welcome the Taskforce’s consideration of how the weaponisation of VAWG fuels harm, misinformation and division in our communities, which ultimately undermines efforts to end and prevent VAWG, and ensure that victims and survivors can access support.

  Tackling gender inequality and misogyny benefits our society as a whole, and is everyone’s business.


Soma Sara, CEO of Everyone’s Invited said:


  Everyone’s Invited welcomes the government’s plans to introduce a Misogyny Taskforce. Sexual violence has long existed in our society, but the growth of dangerous online spaces and the rise of AI have turbocharged the scale and speed of harm.

  Over 53,000 survivors have shared their experiences with us through Everyone’s Invited’s online safe space. For too many, misogyny has profoundly devastated lives.

  We are particularly relieved to see a commitment to prevention through education. Young people need the tools, language and confidence to understand, question and challenge misogyny – online and offline – before it becomes normalised.

  The voices of survivors and young people must be at the heart of this work, and we look forward to working with the Government to ensure this Taskforce delivers meaningful, lasting change.


Felicity Oswald, CEO of Girlguiding said:


  Girlguiding is honoured to join the Minister for Women and Equalities’ new taskforce to tackle misogyny. Girls tell us they are facing rising levels of sexism and misogyny online, in public and in schools. That’s why we are calling for more education around healthy relationships, gender stereotypes, early warning signs and consent.

  We welcome the opportunity to bring girls’ experiences and perspectives directly into discussions with government. Girls are experts in their own lives, and it is vital that their voices are heard when decisions are made that impact them.


Preventing misogyny before it escalates is essential. Nearly 1 million adults experience sexual assault, 1.4 million face stalking, and nearly 4 million endure domestic abuse in a single year. Tackling the source is the only viable path forward. 

This new taskforce comes ahead of further announcement expected from the government this week to step up work to halve violence and women and girls, and is the latest step by this government to use the full power of the state to tackle these vile crimes. 

Last month, the government partnered with the ENOUGH campaign at the Reading and Leeds festivals through powerful messaging raising awareness of abusive behaviours displayed over the weekend. 

The Prime Minister also recently announced that all police forces in England and Wales will have specialist rape and sexual offence teams in place by December 2027 – a year and a half ahead of the original deadline.

The government is also providing a £16 million package to tackle harmful behaviours and attitudes before they escalate, which aims to educate pupils on healthy relationships and train staff to tackle misogyny. Alongside a further £10 million fund to deliver intervention programmes for children actively using harm.

The government also published statutory relationships, sex and health education guidance for schools, challenging myths about women and relationships that are spread online in the “manosphere”.

items.title: Minister for Overseas Territories statement on the Falkland Islands: 18 September
items.summary: The United Kingdom is clear: the Falkland Islands are British and they have the right to develop their natural resources as they see fit. This is an integral part of their right of self-determination. In recent weeks, Argentina has continue
items.bodyHtml:
The United Kingdom is clear: the Falkland Islands are British and they have the right to develop their natural resources as they see fit. This is an integral part of their right of self-determination.

In recent weeks, Argentina has continued to threaten businesses and individuals supplying goods and services, directly and indirectly, to the Falkland Islands, including in the hydrocarbons sector.

The UK Government and our diplomatic network stands fully behind those businesses and individuals. They have our full support. 

This is not the first time that an Argentine Government have made economic threats against the Islanders, yet the Falkland Islands economy continues to flourish.

The UK stands in lockstep with the international community and any attempt to politicise international mechanisms against individuals for doing business with the Falklands are illegitimate. 

These charges against companies and individuals are unacceptable, with no legal justification. 

There are enormous opportunities available for businesses in the Falklands, and we will work tirelessly with the Falkland Islands Government to ensure their wishes are protected.

Media enquiries

Email newsdesk@fcdo.gov.uk

Telephone 020 7008 3100

Email the FCDO Newsdesk (monitored 24 hours a day) in the first instance, and we will respond as soon as possible.

items.title: Funding boost for next generation of British fashion talent
items.summary: £1 million of Government funding to be awarded to emerging talent in fashion design per year for the next 3 years The BFC NEWGEN funding scheme has been run by the British Fashion Council since 1993, with support from Government since 2023,
items.bodyHtml:
• £1 million of Government funding to be awarded to emerging talent in fashion design per year for the next 3 years
  • The BFC NEWGEN funding scheme has been run by the British Fashion Council since 1993, with support from Government since 2023, now extended until 2029
  • Creative Industries Minister attended 26/27 funding recipient Francesca Lake’s showcase to mark the funding announcement

Rising stars in British fashion are set to benefit from £3 million of new funding which aims to launch the career of the next Alexander McQueen or Vivienne Westwood.

The Government has today announced it will continue to fund BFC NEWGEN, the British Fashion Council’s flagship talent support scheme, with £1 million pledged to the next three rounds of the initiative (2026/27, 2027/28, 2028/29).

BFC NEWGEN identifies and nurtures the UK’s most promising fashion designers, providing financial support, mentoring and the chance to showcase collections at London Fashion Week - the biggest event in the UK’s fashion calendar. The event is held every September and February, and is widely considered one of the ‘big four’ global fashion weeks alongside New York, Milan and Paris.

Culture Secretary, Lisa Nandy, said:

Fashion is central to the soul of our country, not just in our economy where it is at the heart of our industrial strategy, but to our cultural identity as a nation. 

We have a proud legacy of iconic fashion houses that have stood the test of time, Burberry, Alexander McQueen, Paul Smith and Vivienne Westwood. I want us to cultivate the next generation of home-grown talent, and schemes like this will help us to nurture the next British fashion powerhouse.

Since its creation in 1993, BFC NEWGEN has supported more than 400 designers and helped launch the careers of some of the world’s most celebrated names, including Alexander McQueen, Jonathan Anderson and Simone Rocha.

The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport has funded the scheme in partnership with the British Fashion Council since 2023, recognising fashion’s importance both as a creative powerhouse and as a major contributor to the UK economy.

To commemorate the funding announcement, Creative Industries Minister Ian Murray joined British Fashion Council CEO Laura Weir at the Francesca Lake showcase, BFC NEWGEN-funded designer who hails from Kingston, Jamaica. Lake’s designs focus on celebrating the untapped stories of her culture and amplifying them on a global scale.

Laura Weir, CEO of the British Fashion Council, said:

We are grateful to the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport for committing to multi-year investment in the BFC NEWGEN programme, recognising the vital role of sustained investment in nurturing the next generation of British fashion talent. The programme has a proven impact on commercial growth, international visibility and the long-term sustainability of designer businesses. This investment will demonstrate what strong, strategic partnerships between Government and the creative industry can achieve, enabling emerging designer businesses to thrive and encouraging good growth in every postcode.

ENDS

Notes to editors

BFC NEWGEN is run by the British Fashion Council with support from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport. 

The funding recipients for 2026/27 are A Letter, Charlie Constantinou, E.W.Usie, Francesca Lake, Gui Rosa, Johanna Parv, Karoline Vitto, Liza Keane, Lueder, Octi, Oscar Ouyang, Pauline Dujancourt, Petra Fagerström, Steve O Smith, The Ouze and Yaku.

ABOUT BRITISH FASHION COUNCIL

The British Fashion Council (BFC), founded in 1983, is a not-for-profit trade association that exists to support, defend and promote British fashion globally, supporting designers and businesses to build creative and commercial resilience.

Through its core platforms, including London Fashion Week and The Fashion Awards, the BFC strengthens the global impact of British fashion, drives cultural relevance, international visibility and industry investment. The Fashion Awards is the world’s biggest fashion fundraiser, raising funds for the BFC Foundation.

Established in 2019, the BFC Foundation (Registered Charity Number: 11852152) underpins the UK’s creative pipeline, supporting creatives from education through to global business growth via its Prizes and Programmes.

Collectively, this work positions British fashion as a driver of the UK’s creative economy and a force in global cultural influence.

items.title: UK’s 250th banking hub opens in Chepstow, keeping access to cash and face-to-face banking in the town
items.summary: Access to cash and face-to-face banking protected in Chepstow as new banking hub opens. The 250th banking hub in the UK will be opened by Treasury Minister Lucy Rigby, keeping a vital service on people’s doorsteps and supporting the growth
items.bodyHtml:
• Access to cash and face-to-face banking protected in Chepstow as new banking hub opens.
  • The 250th banking hub in the UK will be opened by Treasury Minister Lucy Rigby, keeping a vital service on people’s doorsteps and supporting the growth of local businesses.
  • Part of wider work to improve access to banking services across the UK and follows the manifesto commitment to deliver at least 350 banking hubs this parliament.

THOUSANDS of local residents and more than 100 businesses in Chepstow will retain access to cash and essential face-to-face banking services when the UK’s 250th banking hub officially opens town today.

It follows the announced closure of Chepstow’s last remaining bank branch next month, which would see residents having to travel eight miles to Lydney for the nearest branch. That journey can take around 30 minutes by public transport and cost £4, creating a particular barrier for people who rely on nearby in-person services. 

The new banking hub means the ability to deposit and withdraw cash, deposit cheques and access community bankers has been protected for local people – a move that keeps a vital service on people’s doorsteps and supports business growth. The hub also has an external free-to-use ATM to provide 24-hour access to cash for the community. 

Set to be officially opened by the Treasury Minister Lucy Rigby today – the new banking hub is the 250th to be opened since a commitment was made in the manifesto to deliver at least 350 hubs by the end of this parliament. Banking hubs have been opened in other towns across Wales, including Holyhead, Prestatyn and Porthcawl.

Banking hubs are owned by Cash Access UK, the not-for-profit organisation bringing shared cash and banking services to communities across the UK. The hubs provide daily cash counter services for customers to withdraw and deposit cash where traditional bank branches have closed, leaving communities without access to cash. They also provide some wider in-person banking services with multiple high street banks represented in the hubs through rotating community bankers.

Economic Secretary to the Treasury, Rt Hon Lucy Rigby KC MP, said:

This new banking hub means that local residents will still have access to important services they rely on.

We’re well on our way to opening 350 hubs across the UK – a manifesto commitment and a key part of our Financial Inclusion Strategy - which will ensure that people and businesses all over the country have the access to cash and face-to-face banking services they deserve.

Secretary of State for Wales, Rt Hon Stephen Kinnock MP, said:

People and businesses across Wales want services such as banking to be available in their local communities – and that’s what we are delivering via the new hubs.

The UK Government is determined to make local services work better for people, and I’m delighted for the people of Chepstow that this new hub will serve their community so that face-to-face banking continues long into the future.

Gareth Oakley, CEO, Cash Access UK said: 

I’m happy to announce the opening of Chepstow as our 250th hub, ensuring crucial access to cash and face-to-face banking services for residents and businesses across the local community.

The services are hugely popular, with a busy front desk to support cash transactions and a rotating community banker to support face-to-face banking needs. This year we’ve opened a new hub every week, so we see the real difference it makes to the local community and are proud to be bringing this service to Chepstow.

Natalie Ceeney CBE, Chair, Cash Access UK, said:

Every one of our 250 banking hubs exists because millions of people and small businesses across the UK need somewhere to walk in, deposit their takings, withdraw cash, or sit down with someone face to face about their banking.

Since the start of 2026, more than eight million transactions have been supported across all banking hubs and deposit services, showing that face-to-face banking and access to cash is still vital for those that need it. We are working together with the major UK banks to provide this service and will continue to do so in order to support communities across the UK.

This follows the independent Review into Access to Banking Services, commissioned by the UK Government in May, which will examine the impact of changes in access to in-person banking services and identifying whether this is causing detriment to consumers, communities and businesses. The review will make recommendations to Government in October.

items.title: UK galleries urged to save rare Renaissance masterpiece
items.summary: UK galleries given the chance to save the £4.6 million Renaissance masterpiece for the nation Museums and galleries have until 17 December to come forward, helping keep the rare work on public display Galleries and institutions across the U
items.bodyHtml:
• UK galleries given the chance to save the £4.6 million Renaissance masterpiece for the nation
  • Museums and galleries have until 17 December to come forward, helping keep the rare work on public display

Galleries and institutions across the UK have the chance to save Antico’s Seated Nymph for the nation, after the Government temporarily blocked it from leaving the country.

The temporary export bar gives museums and galleries time to raise the £4.6 million needed to acquire the sculpture and keep it in the UK and on public display.

Cast over 500 years ago, the bronze statuette features mercury-gilded hair and drapery, with the exceptional detail and finish for which its sculptor became renowned.

The Seated Nymph was created by Italian sculptor Pier Jacopo Alari Bonacolsi, known as Antico, and is regarded as one of his finest works.

A deadline of 17 December has been set to find a buyer and help keep the rare Renaissance sculpture in the UK and on public display.

The figure stands just under 20cm tall and was likely designed to be held in the hand and turned to be fully appreciated. The tiara on the figure’s head suggests she may represent a goddess, such as Venus.

Arts Minister, Ruth Mackenzie said:

This statuette is small but mighty. The detail and refinement mark it out as an exceptional piece.

I very much hope this export bar can help keep this exquisite statue in the country where the public can also enjoy its beauty.

RCEWA committee member, Stuart Lochhead said: 

Pier Jacopo Alari Bonacolsi, known as Antico, forever linked his fame with his skill at imitating classical antiquity. He developed a highly sophisticated technique for producing luxuriously finished bronze statuettes, becoming one of the leading artists at the court of Mantua. The Seated Nymph is one of his most beautiful creations, embellished with golden hair and drapery, as well as inlaid silver eyes. It was rediscovered in the sculpture collection at Woburn Abbey. The export of this exquisite sculpture from the UK would be a great loss, depriving the public of the work of an exceptionally rare and hugely admired sculptor.

The decision follows the advice of the Reviewing Committee on the Export of Works of Art and Objects of Cultural Interest (RCEWA).

The Committee made its recommendation on the basis that the Seated Nymph by Antico met the second and third Waverley criteria for its outstanding aesthetic importance and its outstanding significance to the study of the history of sculpture collecting in the UK, and within the context of the Bedford collection specifically, and the interrelationship between Antico models.

The decision on the export licence application for the sculpture will be deferred for an initial period ending on 17 December 2026 inclusive in which we welcome expressions of interest from an appropriate purchaser to try and acquire the object. At the end of the first deferral period owners will have a consideration period of 15 Business Days to consider any offer(s) to purchase the sculpture at the recommended price of £4,600,000 (plus VAT of £166,666.67). The second deferral period will commence following the signing of an Option Agreement and will last for five months.

Notes to editors:

  1. Organisations or individuals interested in purchasing the sculpture should contact the RCEWA on 02072680534 or rcewa@artscouncil.org.uk.
  2. Details of the ITEM are as follows: Pier Jacopo Alari Bonacolsi (about 1455-1528), known as Antico, Seated Nymph, about 1503(?). Bronze, with mercury-gilding on the hair and drapery, and silver-inlaid eyes. Height of the figure: 19.5 cm; Height including bronze base: 22 cm
  3. Provenance: [Possibly: Isabella d’Este, Marchioness of Mantua, Castello San Giorgio, Mantua, in 1503, and probably still in the Este family’s possession, Modena, in 1684. Alternatively, possibly: Gianfrancesco Gonzaga, by 1496 (inventory of estate, 8 October 1496, fol. 7r: ‘una figure cum le gambe incrosate de metale’); or Bishop Ludovico Gonzaga (c.1460-1511), or another member of the Gonzaga Family, Mantua, c.1496-11; by descent, until acquired with the Gonzaga collections by King Charles I, 1627/28; sold from the Royal Collection during the Commonwealth Sales, c.1649-54.] The Dukes of Bedford, London and Woburn Abbey, certainly by 1861, [but probably acquired by John Russell, 6th Duke (1766-1839), or an ancestor;] and by descent until sold by the Trustees of the Bedford Estates, Sotheby’s, London, 8 December 2009 (51), where purchased by the present owner.
  4. The Reviewing Committee on the Export of Works of Art and Objects of Cultural Interest is an independent body, serviced by Arts Council England (ACE), which advises the Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport on whether a cultural object, intended for export, is of national importance under specified criteria.

items.title: PM meeting with Micheál Martin the Taoiseach of Ireland: 18 September 2026
items.summary: The Prime Minister met the Taoiseach of Ireland, Micheál Martin today, marking the first time an international leader has visited No10 North. The two leaders began by reaffirming the close partnership between the UK and Ireland, as well as
items.bodyHtml:
The Prime Minister met the Taoiseach of Ireland, Micheál Martin today, marking the first time an international leader has visited No10 North.

The two leaders began by reaffirming the close partnership between the UK and Ireland, as well as their shared commitment to upholding the Good Friday Agreement.

They next discussed the importance of their joint commitments to addressing the legacy of the Troubles and working towards lasting reconciliation in Northern Ireland.

The Prime Minister then underlined the UK’s desire to work closely with Ireland during its presidency of the European Union as the UK seeks a closer relationship with Europe.

On Ukraine, the two leaders were clear in their united support for Ukraine against Russia’s illegal full-scale invasion and their determination to continue working to help Ukraine defend itself against Russian aggression.

They also looked ahead to the UK’s hosting of the next UK-Ireland Summit in the first half of next year and agreed its importance in working together across priorities including security and trade.

They looked forward to meeting in person again soon.
items.bodyText:
The Prime Minister met the Taoiseach of Ireland, Micheál Martin today, marking the first time an international leader has visited No10 North.

The two leaders began by reaffirming the close partnership between the UK and Ireland, as well as their shared commitment to upholding the Good Friday Agreement.

They next discussed the importance of their joint commitments to addressing the legacy of the Troubles and working towards lasting reconciliation in Northern Ireland.

The Prime Minister then underlined the UK’s desire to work closely with Ireland during its presidency of the European Union as the UK seeks a closer relationship with Europe.

On Ukraine, the two leaders were clear in their united support for Ukraine against Russia’s illegal full-scale invasion and their determination to continue working to help Ukraine defend itself against Russian aggression.

They also looked ahead to the UK’s hosting of the next UK-Ireland Summit in the first half of next year and agreed its importance in working together across priorities including security and trade.

They looked forward to meeting in person again soon.

items.title: More enriching activities for hundreds of thousands of children
items.summary: Hundreds of thousands more young people in disadvantaged communities will get the chance to join sports teams, learn an instrument, or take part in debating and outdoor adventures, helping them build confidence, develop new skills and stay
items.bodyHtml:
Hundreds of thousands more young people in disadvantaged communities will get the chance to join sports teams, learn an instrument, or take part in debating and outdoor adventures, helping them build confidence, develop new skills and stay engaged both in and out of education.

More than 400 secondary schools will benefit from tailored support backed by £22.5 million through the government’s Enrichment Expansion programme.

The investment will help schools broaden opportunities for pupils by putting on more activities during the school day or after school ranging from music groups, engineering clubs and debating societies to football teams, volunteering projects and outdoor learning programmes. By building confidence, skills and a sense of belonging, these experiences can help keep young people engaged in education and set them up for future success.

The programme speaks to the findings of the State of the Nation survey of more than 14,000 young people, which found that young people want safe spaces, trusted adults, better mental health support and greater access to enriching activities. Yet too many are still missing out because of where they live or the barriers they face.

Without access to enrichment, too many young people miss out on the confidence, skills and sense of belonging that help them succeed. Those least likely to participate are also more likely to become not in education, employment or training (NEET), making these opportunities a vital part of helping young people stay engaged, raise their aspirations and prepare for future success.

In response, the government launched the Youth Matters Strategy in December last year and committed to halving the participation gap in enriching activities between disadvantaged young people and their peers by 2035. 

Funded by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS), delivered in partnership with the Department for Education (DfE), the Enrichment Expansion programme’s additional funding and support is part of this solution, helping those schools facing the greatest challenges to deliver a wide range of high-quality enrichment opportunities, in line with this year’s new benchmarks for every school.

Schools Minister Georgia Gould said:

A great education is about more than what happens in the classroom. It’s about the football team, the school play, the debate competition, the volunteering project and the outdoor adventure that help young people discover who they are and what they can achieve.

But for too long, too many children have missed out on those opportunities because of where they live or the barriers they face.

This investment will help hundreds of thousands more young people access the activities that build confidence, spark ambition and open up opportunities for the future, helping more children stay on track in education and fulfil their potential.

Both the Enrichment Benchmarks and the Enrichment Expansion programme form part of the government’s mission to ensure that every young person has somewhere to go, something to do and sense of community – including through the recently announced expansion of Young Futures Hubs as well as the £132.5 million Every Child Can programme, which will increase access to a wide range of high-quality activities.

The programme will be delivered by the Youth Sport Trust and a team of national partners, with dedicated Enrichment Co-ordinators managing clusters of local schools to identify gaps in their current offer, develop enrichment plans, and connect with local partners to expand opportunities for their pupils. As part of the funding, schools will receive tailored support to strengthen and grow their enrichment provision, helping more children access high-quality experiences both in and beyond the classroom who otherwise would not have been able to do so.

The investment will support schools to deliver the opportunities outlined in the government’s new Enrichment Benchmarks, announced earlier this year, which provide practical guidance to help every child access high-quality enrichment opportunities as part of their education.

Minister for Young People, Vicky Foxcroft said:

Through our landmark State of a Nation survey we heard from more than 14,000 young people who told us that they feel they are missing out on safe, supportive environments where they can connect with others and find a community to belong to.

Every young person should have somewhere to go, something to do and someone they can trust, where they can discover new interests that help them develop the confidence they need to thrive.

That’s why we’re supporting more than 400 schools to develop their enrichment offers, helping thousands more children access activities and opportunities that build skills, confidence and a stronger sense of belonging.

Supporting delivery of the programme are 5 Enrichment Ambassadorsrepresenting arts and culture, sport and physical activity, nature, outdoors and adventure, civic engagement, and wider life and future skills. Working alongside government, they will champion participation, showcase effective practice and help ensure more children can access high-quality opportunities wherever they live.

Jan Shadick, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Haberdashers’ Academies Trust South, said:

We welcome the government’s new enrichment framework and are proud that today’s launch recognised the excellent work happening at Hatcham College. At Haberdashers’ Academies Trust South, enrichment sits at the heart of the Haberdashers’ Advantage, our character curriculum, ensuring every pupil can develop the knowledge, confidence and character to flourish in school and beyond. We believe these opportunities should be an entitlement for all young people, not a privilege for a few, helping them to become individuals with character who are ready to make a positive contribution to the world around them.

Marcus Davey CBE, Arts and Culture Enrichment Ambassador, said:

Schools are a vital gateway to the creative and enriching experiences that help young people discover their interests, develop confidence and feel a sense of belonging. By strengthening the connections between schools, cultural institutions and local organisations, this programme will help ensure those opportunities reach the young people who stand to benefit most.

Ali Oliver MBE, Chief Executive Officer of Youth Sports Trust, said:

We are honoured and incredibly excited to have been selected to deliver the new Enrichment Expansion Programme. The Youth Sport Trust has long championed the role enrichment can play in the education and development of young people: building belonging and a sense of wellbeing, fostering creativity and passion, and developing skills for learning, life and work. In particular, we are delighted to be collaborating with key partners – ‘Enrichment Builders’ – and together we are determined to help ensure more young people have access to a well-rounded, high-quality enrichment offer which supports the development of new interests, skills and growth through a range of activities. 

We know access to enrichment can have a positive impact across school life, supporting attendance, behaviour and academic achievement. Through the Enrichment Expansion Programme, we want to support the DCMS and DfE in giving more schools the support, opportunities and connections they need to strengthen and broaden their enrichment offer, in particular, helping more disadvantaged young people access opportunities which may otherwise be out of reach.

Today’s announcement is part of the government’s drive to ensure every child can access high-quality enrichment opportunities, regardless of their background or postcode. Reflecting that commitment, today, Schools Minister Georgia Gould is attending the Royal Shakespeare Company’s Building Partnerships: A 20-Year Story symposium, championing the role of arts and culture in helping young people thrive.

items.title: 中国团队研发医疗影像模型 可一次性识别146种腹部病症
items.summary: 中新社杭州9月18日电 (张煜欢)阿里巴巴达摩院与浙江大学医学院附属第一医院等机构研发出通用医疗影像AI模型DAMO RADAR。该模型面向腹部增强CT诊断，可一次性识别146种腹部病症，其准确性首次达到影像科专家级水平，现已正式开源。

items.title: Housing reforms give military families greater say over their homes
items.summary: A new Red Tape Challenge, announced today by the Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, will invite military families to identify and remove outdated housing rules, while new national and regional committees will ensure their experiences directly
items.bodyHtml:
A new Red Tape Challenge, announced today by the Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, will invite military families to identify and remove outdated housing rules, while new national and regional committees will ensure their experiences directly influence future decisions about accommodation services and a ground-breaking pilot will give them a role in signing off repairs to their homes.

The measures build on recent changes already introduced by the Ministry of Defence, including ending outdated restrictions on keeping pets and giving families greater freedom to decorate their homes.

They form part of the Government’s £9.2 billion Defence Housing Strategy, which will transform military housing through the new Defence Housing Service, delivering better homes, improved service standards and a stronger focus on the needs of Service personnel and their families.

Defence Secretary, Wes Streeting MP, said: 

Service families should not feel that decisions about their homes are being made without them. These reforms are about giving families more power and control, with a stronger voice in shaping housing services and a clear route to challenge things that aren’t working.

Alongside major investment in defence housing, we are determined to build a service that listens and delivers the standard of housing our Armed Forces and their families deserve.

A new Code of Conduct will ensure families receive a more consistent and respectful service from everyone representing Defence housing, including contractors across the supply chain.

A new pilot is also being introduced that will give families a greater role in signing off repairs and maintenance work, helping to ensure issues are fully resolved and work is completed to the expected standard before jobs are closed.

A new Customer Committee will also give families a direct voice in decision-making at a national level, while Regional Experience Committees will bring together residents from across the country to identify local issues and help shape future services. Together, the committees will ensure that family feedback informs decisions across the Defence housing system. This shows the government’s commitment to problem-solving and putting power back into local communities.

Tricia Jakeman, Defence Families Champion, whose role it is to listen to Service families and the challenges they are facing, said:

Behind every military home is a family whose support is essential to operational life. Giving Service families a stronger voice in the decisions that affect them is not only the right thing to do, it is essential if we are to deliver the quality of housing and services they deserve.

The changes we’ve seen over the past year show what can be achieved when families are listened to, and this is an important step in ensuring their voices continue to drive positive change.

The Defence Housing Strategy, launched in November, set out the MOD’s plans to reform military housing over the next decade. Backed by £9.2 billion of investment, it will be delivered through the Defence Housing Service, which will be formally established in April 2027.

Service families can find out more about the Red Tape Challenge and submit their suggestions here: Red Tape Challenge

items.title: Taoiseach of Ireland First International Leader to visit No10 North
items.summary: Leaders will discuss further strengthening UK/Ireland relationship across shared objectives including boosting trade, security, and working with the European Union Historic visit follows hosting of Canadian Prime Minister Carney in Liverpoo
items.bodyHtml:
• Leaders will discuss further strengthening UK/Ireland relationship across shared objectives including boosting trade, security, and working with the European Union

  • Historic visit follows hosting of Canadian Prime Minister Carney in Liverpool and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Oxford as PM shines a spotlight on towns up and down the country

The Prime Minister will host the Taoiseach of Ireland, Micheál Martin, in Manchester today (18 September) - the first time an international leader has visited No10 North. 

In their first official meeting since the Prime Minister took office, the two leaders will discuss how the UK and Ireland can cooperate even more closely to create opportunities for people across both countries.

They are expected to focus on shared objectives including boosting trade, supporting Ukraine, and working with the European Union as Ireland continues its presidency of the EU.

The historic visit to No10 North comes as the Prime Minister shines a spotlight on towns up and down the country, days after he hosted Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Liverpool and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte in Oxford.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said:

I’m delighted to be hosting the Taoiseach as the first international leader to visit No10 North – this is a historic moment and a proud day for Manchester. 

No10 North is all about creating opportunities for working people, and our partnership with Ireland as we improve the lives of people in both of our countries is a key part of that.

There is so much we can achieve together: from our shared commitment to the Good Friday Agreement, to trade, to working with Europe and supporting Ukraine. We are the closest of friends, and I look forward to further strengthening that friendship.

Following their meeting at No10 North, the leaders will visit a local Irish community centre to meet with representatives from the Irish community in Greater Manchester, underlining the strong people-to-people links between the UK and Ireland.

Ireland is the UK’s 6th largest trading partner, while Dublin–London is the busiest intra-European air route, highlighting the real, daily benefits the UK-Ireland relationship brings to people in both countries.

The UK government is committed to working with the Irish government to further strengthen this relationship, underpinned by deep historic ties and shared values, as well as the shared Common Travel Area and both countries’ enduring commitment to the Good Friday Agreement.

items.title: Ministers bring together leaders to rewire youth crime prevention
items.summary: Youth Justice Minister Jake Richards convened local leaders and experts in Manchester to tackle youth crime Roundtable explored how greater local leadership could help services work together, intervene earlier and prevent offending Kate Gre
items.bodyHtml:
• Youth Justice Minister Jake Richards convened local leaders and experts in Manchester to tackle youth crime
  • Roundtable explored how greater local leadership could help services work together, intervene earlier and prevent offending
  • Kate Green appointed Expert Adviser on Youth Justice Devolution to help shape government reforms in England

Local leaders and experts from across youth justice, policing, children’s services and education were brought together by the Government in Manchester today (Thursday 17 September) to help shape plans to prevent more young people being drawn into crime.

Youth Justice Minister Jake Richards convened the roundtable alongside Children and Families Minister Josh MacAlister and Policing and Crime Minister Sarah Jones, exploring how services can work better together to identify children at risk earlier - and where giving local and regional leaders greater freedom could help prevent offending and protect victims.

As part of the Government’s drive to take this work forward, Kate Green has been appointed Expert Adviser on Youth Justice Devolution in England, providing independent advice to Ministers on how greater local leadership could improve youth justice and crime prevention.

Her appointment forms part of the Government’s wider ambition to rewire the state, shifting power and accountability from Whitehall to local leaders and giving communities greater freedom to shape services around their needs.

Jake Richards, Youth Justice Minister, said:

Too often, vulnerable children encounter a system where different services are working hard but not always working together. If we are serious about cutting crime, we need to identify those at risk earlier and intervene before they become trapped in a cycle of offending.

Today I brought together local leaders and experts who know their communities best to hear what works and what gets in their way. By breaking down barriers and giving local leaders greater freedom to join up services, we can prevent more young people being drawn into crime and ultimately protect more victims.

The Ministers also visited SHiFT in Manchester earlier in the day, where they met practitioners working intensively with children and young people at the highest risk of entering custody or becoming entrenched in crime.

Ministers saw first-hand how multi-disciplinary, joined-up support can help steer vulnerable young people away from offending.

Children and Families Minister Josh MacAlister said:

Every young person deserves to grow up supported by the adults around them, like teachers and social workers who can help stop them from being drawn into crime.

We need better and earlier intervention for vulnerable children - from the children’s social care system to youth justice. That’s what today’s discussion in Manchester was about: giving local leaders the freedom to build that support around children before it’s too late.

Policing Minister Sarah Jones said:

Every young person deserves the chance to thrive, no matter where they grow up. I have seen first-hand the difference youth services can make to young people. They provide opportunities at times when other doors have shut or a trusted voice when in day-to-day life they may not exist. They can genuinely turn lives round steering people away from crime and giving them hope for the future.

Kate Green, Expert Adviser on Youth Justice Devolution for England, said:

Young people deserve the opportunity to fulfil their potential and that means intervening early, addressing the factors that place them at risk and ensuring services work together effectively around their needs.

I am pleased to be taking on the role of Expert Adviser for England and look forward to supporting ministers and officials as they consider the future of youth justice reform. Today’s roundtable demonstrated the appetite for new approaches, and I am keen to help share evidence, learning and practical experience that can improve outcomes for young people across the country.

Notes to Editors

  • SHiFT Manchester is a partnership between national charity SHiFT, Manchester City Council and the Greater Manchester Violence Reduction Unit. It uses an intensive, relationship-based approach to work with children and young people at the highest risk of entering custody or becoming entrenched in crime.

  • The Government’s “rewiring the state” programme aims to shift power, funding and accountability from Whitehall to local leaders, including by expanding the role of strategic authorities.

  • Kate Green has been appointed Expert Adviser on Youth Justice Devolution for an initial 18-month period. She will advise Ministers on how strategic authorities could play a greater role in youth justice and crime prevention, including joining up services, pooling resources, reducing duplication and strengthening accountability.

  • The Adviser will work with officials across the Ministry of Justice, Home Office and Department for Education. The role is unremunerated.

  • This week saw the announcement of the locations of 42 more Young Futures Hubs, providing mentoring, wellbeing support, trusted adults and positive opportunities for young people in communities affected by violence: Thousands more young people to access help with life’s biggest challenges - GOV.UK

  • The Halving Knife Crime Plan brings together action across Government and society to stop people turning to knife crime and to ensure that perpetrators are caught and brought to justice, including a range of measures that will tackle the root causes of knife crime to ensure young people who are vulnerable to being drawn into crime are identified and offered support in a more systematic way.

Key measures include:

  • Supporting early intervention and prevention by continuing the work of Violence Reduction Units and Young Futures Panel Pilots, backed by over £66 million for the Serious Violence Reduction Programme and the Serious Violence Duty this financial year.

  • Multi-agency Young Futures Panels proactively identify children and referring young people at risk of being drawn into crime connecting them with support earlier. By the end of October 2025, 53 pilot Panels were operational across England and Wales. Pilot Panel delivery has continued in 2026/27, with a further 12 Panels now operational.

Today’s roundtable demonstrated the appetite for new approaches, and I am keen to help share evidence, learning and practical experience that can improve outcomes for young people across the country.


Notes to Editors


  
    SHiFT Manchester is a partnership between national charity SHiFT, Manchester City Council and the Greater Manchester Violence Reduction Unit. It uses an intensive, relationship-based approach to work with children and young people at the highest risk of entering custody or becoming entrenched in crime.
  
  
    The Government’s “rewiring the state” programme aims to shift power, funding and accountability from Whitehall to local leaders, including by expanding the role of strategic authorities.
  
  
    Kate Green has been appointed Expert Adviser on Youth Justice Devolution for an initial 18-month period. She will advise Ministers on how strategic authorities could play a greater role in youth justice and crime prevention, including joining up services, pooling resources, reducing duplication and strengthening accountability.
  
  
    The Adviser will work with officials across the Ministry of Justice, Home Office and Department for Education. The role is unremunerated.
  
  
    This week saw the announcement of the locations of 42 more Young Futures Hubs, providing mentoring, wellbeing support, trusted adults and positive opportunities for young people in communities affected by violence: Thousands more young people to access help with life’s biggest challenges - GOV.UK
  
  
    The Halving Knife Crime Plan brings together action across Government and society to stop people turning to knife crime and to ensure that perpetrators are caught and brought to justice, including a range of measures that will tackle the root causes of knife crime to ensure young people who are vulnerable to being drawn into crime are identified and offered support in a more systematic way.
  


Key measures include:


  
    Supporting early intervention and prevention by continuing the work of Violence Reduction Units and Young Futures Panel Pilots, backed by over £66 million for the Serious Violence Reduction Programme and the Serious Violence Duty this financial year.
  
  
    Multi-agency Young Futures Panels proactively identify children and referring young people at risk of being drawn into crime connecting them with support earlier. By the end of October 2025, 53 pilot Panels were operational across England and Wales. Pilot Panel delivery has continued in 2026/27, with a further 12 Panels now operational.

items.title: Senior Traffic Commissioner launches consultation on local bus service performance standards
items.summary: The consultation seeks views from operators, local authorities, passenger groups and other stakeholders on whether current standards remain fit for purpose and how they should evolve to reflect changes in the industry, legislation and techn
items.bodyHtml:
The consultation seeks views from operators, local authorities, passenger groups and other stakeholders on whether current standards remain fit for purpose and how they should evolve to reflect changes in the industry, legislation and technology.

Statutory Document No. 14, which sets out how traffic commissioners approach regulatory action where services fail to meet expected standards, has not undergone a significant review for over a decade. The review forms part of the Traffic Commissioners’ strategic objective to ensure that statutory guidance remains relevant, proportionate and effective.

Reviewing bus punctuality and reliability standards

The consultation focuses in particular on whether the longstanding expectation that 95% of services operate within a window of one minute early to five minutes late remains appropriate in 2026

It also explores:

  • how standards should apply to different types of services, including frequent and flexible routes
  • what constitutes a ‘reasonable excuse’ for poor performance
  • what positive actions by operators should be recognised as mitigation

In addition, the call for evidence considers whether clearer guidance is needed where performance falls below expectations, including the role of improvement plans before formal regulatory action is taken.

Wider regulatory considerations

The consultation also seeks views on a range of related regulatory matters, including:

  • Compliance with Bus Open Data obligations: how traffic commissioners should respond where operators fail to meet their obligations under the Public Service Vehicles (Open Data) (England) Regulations 2020
  • Traffic management: how powers under the Traffic Management Act 2004 could be used to obtain information from local authorities where network issues affect service performance
  • Franchising arrangements: the appropriate regulatory response where services operate without the required authority in franchised areas

The consultation also examines how emerging technology, such as real-time passenger information, and evolving operating environments should influence regulatory expectations.

Collaboration and future standards

The Senior Traffic Commissioner has already engaged with stakeholders in developing the proposals and is now inviting broader input to help shape future guidance.

The aim is to ensure that the regulatory framework:

  • supports reliable and efficient local bus services
  • reflects modern operating conditions
  • promotes fairness and consistency across the industry

Kevin Rooney, Senior Traffic Commissioner for Great Britain, said

“Local bus services play a vital role in connecting communities and supporting economic activity. It is important that our regulatory approach keeps pace with changes in the industry and continues to promote reliable and high-quality services for passengers.

“This consultation provides an opportunity for all stakeholders to share their views on how performance standards should be applied in the future. I encourage anyone with an interest to contribute.”

How to respond

The consultation is open to responses from individuals and organisations. Stakeholders are invited to submit their views on any of the questions set out in the document.

Responses can be submitted by email or post, with full details provided in the Local bus service performance standards: consultation - GOV.UK.

The evidence gathered will inform updates to statutory guidance and statutory directions issued by the Senior Traffic Commissioner.

items.title: DBS launches campaign to help parents and carers make informed decisions when hiring self-employed workers
items.summary: Parents and carers across England, Wales, the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man are being encouraged to take an additional safeguarding step when hiring self-employed workers and personal employees, as the Disclosure and Barring Service (
items.bodyHtml:
Parents and carers across England, Wales, the Channel Islands and the Isle of Man are being encouraged to take an additional safeguarding step when hiring self-employed workers and personal employees, as the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) launches its new Every Check Helps public awareness campaign.

The campaign aims to help parents and carers understand what information may be available when employing someone such as a tutor, sports coach, music teacher, personal assistant or carer, and how that information can support safer recruitment and safeguarding decisions.

The campaign follows legislative changes introduced in January 2026, which enabled eligible self-employed workers and personal employees to apply for Enhanced DBS checks and, where eligible, Enhanced DBS checks with Children’s and/or Adults’ Barred List checks for the first time.

Research and stakeholder insight identified that many parents and carers are unaware that eligible self-employed workers can obtain an Enhanced DBS check, and some may feel unsure about asking to see one when making recruitment decisions. The campaign aims to increase awareness, understanding and confidence among parents and carers, helping them make safer and more informed choices.

At the heart of the campaign is a simple message: “They can get a DBS check. You can ask to see it.” The campaign encourages parents and carers to consider DBS information as one part of a wider decision-making process when choosing someone to work with their child or vulnerable family member.

Importantly, parents and carers cannot apply for a DBS check on behalf of someone else. Where eligible, self-employed workers and personal employees must apply themselves through a DBS Umbrella Body. Parents and carers can then ask whether an individual has a DBS certificate and whether they are willing to share it.

Alongside the campaign, DBS has published guidance explaining what parents and carers should look for when viewing a DBS certificate, including checking they are seeing the original certificate, confirming it relates to the correct workforce, checking the certificate issue date and understanding how the DBS Update Service may provide additional reassurance.

The guidance is designed to help parents and carers better understand what they can do, what they should look for on a DBS certificate and how DBS information can be considered alongside other recruitment and safeguarding considerations.

Minister for Safeguarding and Violence Against Women and Girls, Satvir Kaur said:

As a mother, I know how important it is to feel confident about the people we trust with our children. 

With self-employed people who work with children now able to get enhanced checks, parents and carers will have options to make the safest choice for their families.

It’s part of this Government’s ongoing work to keep children safe, backed by record funding and stronger laws.

Susie Blamire, Associate Director – Strategic Lead for Safeguarding at DBS said: 

The introduction of Enhanced DBS checks for eligible self-employed workers is an important step forward. It means that tutors, coaches, music teachers, carers and others working independently can now provide additional safeguarding information.

A DBS certificate is only one part of the picture, but it can be a valuable part. It should be considered alongside references, recommendations, qualifications, experience, and personal judgement to help build a fuller understanding of an individual’s suitability.

Every question asked and every piece of information considered can contribute to safer decisions and better protection for children and vulnerable people.

Parents and carers are encouraged to review the guidance on GOV.UK to better understand what DBS information may be available, how it can support informed decision-making and what to look for when someone chooses to share a DBS certificate.

Background

  • From 21 January 2026, eligible self-employed workers and personal employees became able to apply for Enhanced DBS checks and, where eligible, Enhanced DBS checks with Children’s and/or Adults’ Barred List checks.
  • The Every Check Helps campaign aims to help parents and carers make informed decisions when hiring individuals to work with their child or vulnerable family member.
  • Parents and carers cannot apply for a DBS check on someone else’s behalf. Eligible individuals must apply themselves through a DBS Umbrella Body.
  • An Enhanced DBS certificate should be considered alongside references, qualifications, experience, recommendations and personal judgement.
  • Campaign resources include GOV.UK guidance, a parent and carer leaflet, partner communications materials and practical advice on what to check when viewing a DBS certificate.
